summary: Removes the element at index a2 from a packed record array rooted at a1: when a2 is not the final element it shifts the array tail down by one record by copying the byte span a1[2] * (count - a2 - 1) from element a2 + 1 onto element a2 via sub_58B130, then decrements the stored count at a1[0] and returns the new count. The single caller NetworkConnection suggests the array is a connection/record list that shrinks when an entry is dropped.

local_names.a1: packed record array; a1[0] is the element count and a1[2] the byte stride per record
local_names.a2: index of the element to remove
local_names.v4: ecx this pointer equal to a1, reused as the first argument of the second LinearInterpolation call
local_names.v7: address of element a2 + 1 resolved by LinearInterpolation
local_names.v5: address of element a2 resolved by LinearInterpolation
local_names.v8: byte span of the tail being shifted: a1[2] * (count - a2 - 1)

operations.description: Proceed with the shift only when the removal index a2 is strictly less than the last valid index *a1 - 1, i.e. a2 is not the final element.
Compute the byte span v8 = a1[2] * (*a1 - a2 - 1), the size of the contiguous tail starting at element a2 + 1.
Resolve the address of element a2 + 1 as v7 = LinearInterpolation(a1, a2 + 1).
Resolve the address of element a2 as v5 = LinearInterpolation(v4, a2), where v4 is the ecx this pointer equal to a1.
Shift the tail into the removed slot by calling sub_58B130(v5, v7, v8): v8 bytes copied from element a2 + 1 onto element a2 (memmove-like block move).
Decrement the stored element count: result = *a1 - 1; *a1 = result.

unresolved: a1[2] is assumed to be the per-record byte stride; the packet provides no name evidence, only its use in the byte-span arithmetic.
LinearInterpolation is the Hex-Rays symbol; its role as an element-address/offset resolver is DERIVED from the call pattern.
sub_58B130 is presumed to be a byte-block copy/move (memmove-like); its exact contract is not evidenced in this packet.
Why the caller NetworkConnection (0x00563260) removes array elements, and what the array holds, is not derivable here.
v4 is uninitialized in the decompiled listing and is interpreted as the ecx this pointer equal to a1, a DERIVED assumption.
